question: Which key picks up the Component insert tool?
context: The UI design mock puts a Component insert tool after Frame with the key C. In Photonz, as in Photoshop, C is Crop, and the house rule is one letter per tool everywhere. The tool is built and in the Design tool bar on N for now.

options.label: N everywhere, C stays Crop
options.summary: The Component insert tool answers to N in every mode and every document, and its tip reads Component insert N. C crops, as it does in Photoshop, wherever you are. This is what is built now.
pros: One letter means one tool everywhere, so a key you learned never changes under you
Photoshop leaves N unassigned and no Photonz tool uses it, so nothing moves
Crop keeps the C every Photoshop user reaches for
cons: The mock prints C, so the tip and the mock disagree
N has no link to the word component
options.mitigation: The tip on the button and its rows under More and in Edit > Tools all print N, so the letter is taught wherever the tool is seen.

options.label: C in Design, Crop has no letter there
options.summary: In the Design mode C picks up Component insert, as the mock draws it, and Crop (which sits under More in Design) has no letter there. In every other mode C crops as it does today and Component insert answers to nothing.
cons: C means two different tools depending on the mode, and a person pressing C to crop a screenshot in Design gets a component tool instead
Component insert has no key at all outside Design
options.mitigation: The tips and Edit > Tools rows would print whichever letter the current mode gives, so the menu never lies about what C does right now.

options.label: Q everywhere, C stays Crop
options.summary: The Component insert tool answers to Q in every mode, and C stays Crop. On a video, while the timeline has the keyboard, Q keeps trimming the clip start to the playhead as in Premiere; a click on the canvas gives Q back to the tool.
pros: One letter, one tool on the canvas
Leaves N free for the mock prototyping Connect tool when it is built
cons: Q is Quick Mask in Photoshop, which Photonz may want later
Q shares the timeline ripple trim key on a video, like L, I and O already do
options.mitigation: The same rule the timeline already uses for I, O and L: the keyboard follows where you last clicked, and the accent ring says which.
